script: What would happen if 2 players were TIED for the Ballon d'Or? So the Ballon d'Or voting works like this. 100 judges from around the world each pick their top 10 players and rank them, where your first pick gets 15 points, second gets 12, third gets 10, and it keeps going down all the way to 1 point for 10th place. Add up all the points, and whoever has the most wins. Now, let's say 2 players end up with the exact same total. The first thing they check is who got more first-place votes. So if both players scored 847 points and Player A got 32 first-place votes while Player B only got 28, Player A wins. If they're still tied after that, they move to whoever gets the most second place votes, then third place votes, then fourth, literally going through every single ranking until someone comes out ahead. But what if 2 players are perfectly tied on all of that? Well, first, if you're enjoying the video, please hit the follow button. Second of all, with 100 journalists voting across 10 spots each, the chances of 2 players matching on total points and every single voting position is very close to being mathematically impossible. But if it somehow did happen, the editor-in-chief of France Football just picks the winner themselves, and you can't appeal it.
